source_text: Legends: P1- Standing, P2- Standing in middle, P3 -Kneeling, P4- Sitting, P5- Sitting middle, P6- Rampant, P7- Turning, P8- Charging, P9- Sideways, P10- Dominant P11- Aggressive/Combative, P12- x 2 and facing, P13- x 2 and facing away, P14- Waving, P15- Horn +/-, P16- Special tail, P17- Fused, P18- Joined @ neck, P19- Joined @ centre, P20- Stage marker; F0- Always free, F-- Occasionally free, F1- Feeding/foraging/browsing, ImF1- Implicit F1; F2- Mystery object, ImF2- Implicit F2; F3- Frontal sign; b- object in front broken off; p-partial stamping of an impression; i-identical faces; Terminal X- No sign; Terminal X- - Sign obliterated; S- one or more signs on two or more faces of a seal-impression; Si- Identical sign sequence across faces of a seal-impression. S1 series- sequences on seal impressions. U1 series- sequences on seals. All sequences are reported right to left and in the face order given by CISI. When columns ‘right’ and ‘left’ are merged, it denotes that symbol or compound is adirectional. L- Left orientation.

Notes: The focus on instruments of reproduction and mass production makes some exclusions necessary. These are listed below.  
Zoomorphism on what CISI calls incised tablets is excluded as the expression can be one-off, ad hoc, and non-standard. The incised “miniature tablets” from the lower levels of Harappa are known to be the earliest examples of the fully developed Indus script, which then give way to the embossed ones that are often mass-produced in moulds (Shah and Parpola 1987: XVI). Incised tablets are not intended for stamped reproduction as is certainly the case with inscribed seals. Their contents are read straight and not from their mirrored impressions.
Cylinder seals and impressions thereof are excluded, as their total count does not attain two digits (CISI).
The study glosses over related morphisms, anthropo-, phyto- and geometric, and does not feature them in the tabulation unless they occur on an object that features an animal.
There are some entries in CISI where the zoomorphism is not entirely legible, noted in a row with the label: Illegible.
The grouping in CISI of the Indus unicorn seals into six types based on seal dimensions, and their sub-grouped arrangement by stylistic criteria whose “basic scheme was developed by Paul Rissman” (Joshi and Parpola 1987: XXXII) is not linked to any particular design motive or technique proposed in this paper.
